To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate a CEP stabilized OPA in the mid infrared from 2.8 to 3.7 mm, with a pulse energy up to 56 mW, pulse durations of 100 fs and a root mean square CEP error of 100 mrad.
we demonstrated the generation of mid infrared pulses with CEP control in a wavelength range from 2.8 to 4 mm.
we demonstrated an efficient and robust mid-infrared OPA seeded with sub-two-cycle pulses generated by intra-pulse DFG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and characterization of mid infrared pulses in the wavelength region from 2.8 to 3.9 mm.
the development of high energy mid infrared laser pulses with sub two cycle duration for applications in high field science and molecular dynamics.
the development of an ultrafast laser source for high order harmonic generation (HHG).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented results show the potential of the OPA to generate CEP stabilized pulses at the mid-infrared wavelength range.
a CEP stabilized OPA system from 2.5 to 3.5 mm is developed and characterized, which will be used in a pump-probe experiment to investigate carrier dynamics in semiconductors.
the OPA output energy and temporal width are 1.7 times and half of those obtained by the previous OPA using a 2.7 mJ CEP stabilized pulse at 2.7 mm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CEP stabilized mid IR OPA is a promising tool to investigate ultrafast dynamics and to perform high resolution spectroscopy in the mid IR region.
the combination of intra pulse DFG with CEP stabilized pulses and a wavelength tunable OPA is an effective method for producing CEP stabilized mid IR pulses.
we have developed a compact, high average power, high energy and high repetition rate CEP stabilized mid-infrared laser system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CEP of the OPA pulses is well preserved, and the CEP error is only slightly affected by the OPA process.

CEP stabilized mid-IR pulses can be produced by a compact, robust, and cost efficient setup, which can be used in various applications such as high harmonic generation, attosecond science and strong field physics.
CEP stabilized mid-infrared pulses can be generated by intra pulse DFG and amplified in an OPA.
